verdict.rationale: Both PRs make the same core fix: a Map from normalized email to the first index, updated as new contacts are appended. This keeps first-match semantics, arrival order, and merging of duplicates within the upload. B adds a test pinning the duplicate-in-existing edge case and a 30k-into-50k scale test that would catch a regression back to quadratic behavior. A adds no tests for the changed behavior. B also reports running the typecheck, and its `undefined` check is slightly cleaner than A's `?? -1` sentinel.
a_issues: No tests added. The claim that a duplicate email already in the address book still merges into the first entry is unprotected, and nothing guards against a performance regression.
The `?? -1` sentinel keeps the old findIndex convention instead of checking `undefined` directly, which is slightly less clear.
The report does not mention running `tsc --noEmit`.
b_issues: The wall-clock assertion (<2000ms) in a unit test can be flaky on slow or loaded CI machines, though the threshold is generous.
The closing remark that any remaining slowness must come from parsing is speculation, not something it measured.

verdict.rationale: Both changes add the same Map index of the first entry per normalized email and keep first-match, append-order and in-upload duplicate merging, so their code is equivalent and correct. A also adds a test that pins first-entry-wins when the existing book has duplicates, which is the subtle semantic the rewrite could break. It adds a 30k-into-50k timing test as well, which guards against the quadratic scan returning. B adds no tests, so the new indexing logic is protected only by the existing suite.
a_issues: The wall-clock timing test (under 2000 ms) can be flaky on slow CI machines, though the threshold is generous.
The closing remark in the report that parsing may be the remaining bottleneck is speculative and was not measured.
b_issues: No tests cover the new index-based lookup, including first-entry-wins when the existing book has duplicate emails and protection against a performance regression.
`indexByEmail.get(key) ?? -1` maps back to the old -1 sentinel, which is slightly less direct than checking for undefined.
